trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Edinburgh
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Edinburgh Trams service from the airport directly to the city centre (approx. £7.50 one-way). Check in to your Old Town accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour — after settling in, head straight out to explore the Royal Mile on foot. This self-guided or low-cost guided walk runs from Edinburgh Castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Take in landmarks like St Giles' Cathedral, the Real Mary King's Close exterior, and the Scottish Parliament building. The walk is largely free and perfectly located from your Old Town base.
day_by_day.evening: Underground Vaults & Ghost Tour — as dusk falls, join one of the atmospheric evening tours of the South Bridge Vaults. Several operators (such as Mercat Tours or Auld Reekie Tours) offer tickets from around £12–£16 per person. A brilliant and budget-friendly introduction to Edinburgh's dark history.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — Pret a Manger or a local café near your accommodation.
meals.lunch: Oink on the Royal Mile — famous for their hog roast rolls from around £5–£7. Perfect fuel for the afternoon walk.
meals.dinner: Mum's Great Comfort Food (Forrest Road, near Old Town) — hearty Scottish comfort food at very reasonable prices, mains from around £8–£12.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive prepared for September weather — mild but potentially rainy. Pack a light waterproof jacket. Buy a city map or download the Visit Edinburgh app for free navigation. Book the Ghost Tour in advance online to secure a spot and sometimes get a small discount.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour — head up the Royal Mile first thing to beat the crowds. The castle opens at 09:30. Adult tickets are around £17–£19 (book online in advance to save a little). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, the Great Hall, and the stunning panoramic views over the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience — conveniently located right next to Edinburgh Castle on Castlehill, this is an ideal afternoon follow-on. The standard barrel ride tour and tasting costs around £17–£20 per person and covers the history and regions of Scotch whisky in an engaging, immersive way. A must-do for whisky enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket area — wander down to this historic square at the foot of the castle. Browse the independent shops and enjoy the lively atmosphere. In the evening, visit The Bow Bar on West Bow for an outstanding selection of Scottish whiskies by the glass from around £4–£8 per dram — one of Edinburgh's best traditional pubs.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee (South College Street) — excellent coffee and affordable pastries or granola bowls from around £3–£6.
meals.lunch: Canteen at the Scotch Whisky Experience includes light bites, or grab a budget lunch at Greggs or a local bakery on the Royal Mile for under £5.
meals.dinner: The Grassmarket Restaurant or Biddy Mulligans in Grassmarket — pub grub with mains from around £9–£13. Try the Cullen skink or Scottish beef stew.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is activity-heavy and involves a lot of walking uphill. Wear comfortable shoes. Pre-book both the Castle and Whisky Experience online to save time and potentially money. The Scotch Whisky Experience sometimes offers combo deals — check their website.

day_by_day.morning: Arthur's Seat Hike — take a free morning hike up to the summit of Arthur's Seat in Holyrood Park, an ancient volcano rising 251 metres above the city. The hike takes about 45–60 minutes and rewards you with breathtaking views across Edinburgh and the Firth of Forth. Completely free and one of the best experiences the city offers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palace of Holyroodhouse exterior and grounds — at the base of Arthur's Seat, walk around the Palace of Holyroodhouse (official Scottish residence of the monarch). If budget allows, entry to the palace is around £16–£18, but the surrounding grounds and abbey ruins can be viewed from outside for free. Then stroll back up the Royal Mile stopping into St Giles' Cathedral (free entry, donations welcome).
day_by_day.evening: Whisky tasting at a specialist bar — visit Whiski Rooms on the Royal Mile or The Scotch Whisky Society (if you can access a guest pass). Whiski Rooms offers curated tasting flights from around £15–£25 for 3–5 drams with tasting notes — a fantastic deep-dive for whisky lovers on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Pick up supplies from a Lidl or Co-op (there is one near Old Town) the night before — bread, fruit, and yoghurt for a self-catered breakfast to save money.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch taken up Arthur's Seat, or grab a sandwich and snacks from a supermarket for under £4.
meals.dinner: The Elephant House Café (George IV Bridge) — famously where J.K. Rowling wrote early Harry Potter drafts. Affordable meals and snacks from £7–£12, with great atmosphere and history.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Arthur's Seat hike early in the morning to avoid crowds and catch the best light. The path can be slippery if wet — wear trainers or walking shoes. Bring water. September mornings can be cool so layer up.

day_by_day.morning: National Museum of Scotland — spend the morning at this world-class museum on Chambers Street, just a short walk from Old Town. Entry is completely FREE. Explore Scottish history from prehistoric times through the Jacobite era, industrial revolution, and beyond. The Scottish history galleries are exceptional and directly complement your interest in the city's past.
day_by_day.afternoon: Greyfriars Kirkyard and Old Town exploration — visit the famous Greyfriars Kirkyard (free entry), resting place of many historical figures and inspiration for Greyfriars Bobby. Explore the surrounding Cowgate and Candlemaker Row. Then visit the Scottish Storytelling Centre on the Royal Mile (free exhibitions) and browse the closes (alleyways) off the Royal Mile such as Advocates Close and Riddles Court.
day_by_day.evening: Live traditional Scottish music session — head to Sandy Bell's pub on Forrest Road or The Royal Oak on Infirmary Street. Both are legendary folk music pubs that host free live traditional music sessions most evenings. Enjoy a pint of Scottish ale (around £4–£5) and soak in authentic Edinburgh atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café Lucano on George IV Bridge — budget-friendly full Scottish breakfast or continental option from around £5–£8.
meals.lunch: Mosque Kitchen on Nicolson Square — legendary Edinburgh institution serving generous portions of curry, rice, and naan for around £5–£7. Hugely popular with students and locals alike.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from a supermarket (Lidl or Sainsbury's Local on Nicolson Street) — pick up Scottish cheeses, oatcakes, cold meats, and a small bottle of Scottish ale for a budget feast under £8.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evening in Edinburgh is lively — book a table for dinner if eating out. Sandy Bell's and The Royal Oak do not charge for music — just buy a drink. The National Museum of Scotland can easily fill a full morning; arrive at opening (10:00) to make the most of it.

day_by_day.morning: Calton Hill — climb Calton Hill (free) for panoramic views over Edinburgh, the castle, Arthur's Seat, and the Firth of Forth. Visit the National Monument (Scotland's unfinished Parthenon), the Nelson Monument, and the City Observatory. A wonderful final morning activity with great photo opportunities. Then walk through Princes Street Gardens at the foot of the castle — free and beautifully maintained.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whisky shopping on the Royal Mile — browse specialist whisky shops such as Royal Mile Whiskies or Cadenhead's Whisky Shop (Scotland's oldest independent bottler, established 1842). Even on a budget, you can pick up a miniature or an affordable bottle as a souvenir. Staff are knowledgeable and happy to give recommendations without pressure to buy. Then enjoy a final leisurely walk through Old Town to say goodbye to your favourite spots.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and a final dram — treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent farewell meal (still budget-conscious) at The Last Drop in Grassmarket (mains £10–£15, great atmosphere in a historic building). Follow with a final whisky at The Bow Bar or Whiski Rooms, choosing a dram that represents your favourite region discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Söderberg Bakery on Quartermile — Scandinavian-style bakery with excellent pastries and coffee from around £4–£7. A local favourite.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Princes Street Gardens — grab supplies from a nearby Pret, Greggs, or supermarket and enjoy the stunning views of the castle. Under £6.
meals.dinner: The Last Drop, Grassmarket — hearty Scottish pub food in a historic setting. Two courses with a drink for around £18–£22 per person as a fitting budget-friendly farewell.

day_by_day.notes: If departing by flight, check airport transfer times — the tram from York Place (St Andrew Square) to Edinburgh Airport takes approximately 35 minutes and costs around £7.50. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your departure time. Calton Hill is best visited in the morning light. Saturday markets may be running near the Grassmarket — worth a browse for local produce and crafts.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Edinburgh Trams service from the airport to the city centre (approx. 30 min, ~£7). Check in to your Old Town accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour: After settling in, join the early afternoon walking tour along the famous Royal Mile. Starting near Edinburgh Castle Esplanade and winding down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse, this self-guided or guided tour introduces you to closes, wynds, and centuries of Scottish history. Perfect for getting your bearings in the Old Town neighbourhood right on your doorstep.
day_by_day.evening: Scotch Whisky Experience: Head to the Scotch Whisky Experience on Castlehill (a short walk from the Royal Mile). The evening session includes an immersive barrel-ride journey through whisky-making history and a tasting of regional Scotch styles. A brilliant first-night introduction to one of Scotland's greatest exports.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — nothing formal scheduled given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Deacon's House Café on the Royal Mile: a cosy, mid-range café serving traditional Scottish soups, toasties, and light bites. Budget ~£10–14.
meals.dinner: The Witchery by the Castle (bar menu): Atmospheric Old Town restaurant steps from the castle. Order from the more affordable bar menu — Scottish smoked salmon, haggis bon bons, and a dram. Budget ~£25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: September in Edinburgh can be cool and breezy (12–17°C typical). Pack a light waterproof layer. The Scotch Whisky Experience should be booked in advance online to secure an evening slot.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour: Spend the morning exploring the iconic fortress perched on Castle Rock. Highlights include the Scottish Crown Jewels (Honours of Scotland), the Stone of Destiny, St Margaret's Chapel, and sweeping city panoramas. Arrive early (doors open 09:30) to beat crowds. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Tickets ~£18–22 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whisky Tasting at The Whiski Rooms: After the castle, walk down the Royal Mile to The Whiski Rooms on North Bank Street. Enjoy a curated guided tasting of five premium Scotch whiskies — Highlands, Speyside, Islay, and more — led by a knowledgeable whisky specialist. A perfect complement to last night's Scotch Whisky Experience, this time focusing on hands-on tasting. Session ~90 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket neighbourhood below the castle. Browse independent shops, enjoy the lively atmosphere, and take a leisurely evening stroll around Greyfriars Kirkyard — one of Edinburgh's most atmospheric historic graveyards, free to enter.

meals.breakfast: Café Marlayne on the Royal Mile or your hotel — continental breakfast with fresh coffee. Budget ~£8–12.
meals.lunch: The Grain Store on Victoria Street: A mid-range Scottish bistro with excellent seasonal lunch menus. Try the cullen skink (smoked haddock chowder) or a Scottish beef burger. Budget ~£14–18.
meals.dinner: The Last Drop pub in the Grassmarket: Historic pub with hearty Scottish pub food — steak pie, fish and chips, and local ales. Relaxed, mid-range atmosphere. Budget ~£16–22.

day_by_day.notes: Book Edinburgh Castle tickets online in advance to avoid queues. The Whiski Rooms tasting sessions also benefit from advance reservation. Victoria Street (near Grassmarket) is said to have inspired Diagon Alley — worth a wander.

day_by_day.morning: Arthur's Seat Hike: Take a morning walk up Arthur's Seat, the ancient volcanic peak rising above the city in Holyrood Park. The main route from Holyrood takes approximately 45–60 minutes to summit. Rewarded with panoramic views of Edinburgh, the Firth of Forth, and the Pentland Hills. Free, and a wonderful contrast to the urban sightseeing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palace of Holyroodhouse: Descend from Arthur's Seat directly to the Palace of Holyroodhouse at the foot of the Royal Mile — the official Scottish residence of the British monarch. Explore the State Apartments, the ruins of Holyrood Abbey, and the chambers associated with Mary Queen of Scots. Audio guide included. Tickets ~£17–20.
day_by_day.evening: Underground Vaults & Ghost Tour: After dark, join the Underground Vaults & Ghost Tour beneath South Bridge. Descend into the 18th-century vaults with a costumed guide recounting tales of body snatchers, plague victims, and paranormal activity. One of Edinburgh's most atmospheric experiences. Tours typically depart 19:00–21:30.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee on South College Street: Specialty coffee and excellent breakfast rolls or avocado toast. Budget ~£8–11. Fuel up before the hike.
meals.lunch: Picnic provisions from Valvona & Crolla deli on Elm Row (or a local bakery) enjoyed near Holyrood Park, or grab a light bite at the Palace café. Budget ~£8–12.
meals.dinner: Ondine Restaurant on George IV Bridge: Award-winning Scottish seafood — sustainably sourced oysters, langoustines, and fish. Slightly splurge-worthy but well within mid-range for a special evening. Budget ~£30–40.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for Arthur's Seat — the path can be uneven and slippery if damp. The Ghost Tour is suitable for adults and older teens; book in advance as popular slots sell out. September evenings get dark by 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: New Town Exploration & Scottish National Portrait Gallery: Cross Princes Street into Edinburgh's Georgian New Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the Scottish National Portrait Gallery on Queen Street — free entry — featuring portraits of Mary Queen of Scots, Bonnie Prince Charlie, Robert Burns, and other Scottish icons. Beautifully restored Victorian Gothic building. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whisky Shop Trail & Distillery Visit: Spend the afternoon on a self-guided whisky trail. Visit The Scotch Malt Whisky Society members' room on Queen Street for a relaxed dram, then head to the Edinburgh Gin Distillery or the nearby Holyrood Distillery (Edinburgh's first single malt distillery in over 100 years) for a guided tour and tasting. Holyrood Distillery tour ~£15–20.
day_by_day.evening: Calton Hill at Sunset: Climb Calton Hill (a gentle 10-minute walk from Princes Street) for golden-hour views over the city, the Firth of Forth, and Arthur's Seat. Free and spectacular in September evening light. Afterwards, enjoy a relaxed dinner in the New Town.

meals.breakfast: The Edinburgh Larder on Blackfriars Street: Beloved local café known for Scottish produce — porridge with honey, smoked salmon bagels, and excellent filter coffee. Budget ~£9–13.
meals.lunch: Dishoom Edinburgh on St Andrew Square: Bombay-inspired café with exceptional black dal, bacon naan rolls, and chai. Hugely popular — arrive early or expect a short queue. Budget ~£14–18.
meals.dinner: The Bon Vivant on Thistle Street: Cosy New Town wine bar and bistro with a seasonal Scottish menu and excellent whisky list. Try the lamb rump or pan-seared sea trout. Budget ~£22–30.

day_by_day.notes: The Scottish National Portrait Gallery is free — a great mid-trip cultural anchor. Holyrood Distillery tours should be booked in advance. Dishoom does not take reservations for smaller groups so arrive before 12:30 to minimise waiting.

day_by_day.morning: Victoria Street & Grassmarket Markets: On Saturday morning, explore the colourful curve of Victoria Street with its independent boutiques and speciality shops. Browse any local weekend market stalls around the Grassmarket. Pick up Scottish souvenirs — shortbread, tartan, and of course a bottle of Scotch from one of the specialist whisky shops such as Royal Mile Whiskies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Museum of Edinburgh & Canongate Kirk: Visit the Museum of Edinburgh on the Royal Mile (free entry) for a deep dive into the city's social history, including the original National Covenant document and artefacts from across the centuries. Nearby, explore Canongate Kirk and its historic kirkyard where economist Adam Smith is buried. A reflective, unhurried final afternoon in the Old Town.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Dram: Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner at a classic Edinburgh restaurant, followed by a nightcap whisky at The Bow Bar on West Bow — a traditional pub with one of the finest selections of single malts in the city, served without pretension at honest prices.

meals.breakfast: Peter's Yard on Quartermile: Scandinavian-inspired bakery with outstanding sourdough, cardamom buns, and great coffee. A relaxed final morning treat. Budget ~£9–12.
meals.lunch: Mums Great Comfort Food on Forrest Road: Edinburgh institution serving elevated Scottish comfort classics — haggis, neeps & tatties, macaroni pie, and irresistible puddings. Budget ~£12–16.
meals.dinner: The Outsider on George IV Bridge: Consistently excellent mid-range restaurant with a creative Scottish menu and great wine list. Mains include venison, halibut, and seasonal vegetarian options. Budget ~£25–35. Follow with a dram at The Bow Bar (~£5–8 per whisky).

day_by_day.notes: Royal Mile Whiskies is an excellent specialist retailer for taking home a bottle — staff can advise based on your tastings during the week. Check your flight details for Day 6 departure and arrange an airport transfer or tram the evening before if flying early. The Bow Bar closes around midnight on Saturdays.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private chauffeur transfer arranged from the airport to your luxury accommodation in Old Town Edinburgh. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour: After settling in, embark on a private guided walk along the iconic Royal Mile, stretching from Edinburgh Castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Your expert guide will uncover centuries of history, hidden closes, and fascinating stories of Old Town Edinburgh — the perfect orientation to the city on your first afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Scotch Whisky Experience: Begin your whisky journey with an immersive early-evening tour at the Scotch Whisky Experience on Castlehill, just steps from the castle. Featuring a barrel ride through the history of Scotch and a tutored tasting of premium single malts, this sets the tone for the whisky-focused days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the flight or a light arrival snack at the airport's premium lounge.
meals.lunch: The Witchery by the Castle — a legendary Edinburgh institution at the top of the Royal Mile, serving refined Scottish cuisine in a dramatic Gothic setting. Perfect for a luxurious first lunch.
meals.dinner: Ondine Restaurant — an award-winning seafood restaurant on George IV Bridge, celebrated for its sustainably sourced Scottish seafood and outstanding wine list. Reserve the chef's table for an intimate premium experience.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private chauffeur in advance for the airport transfer. The Royal Mile Walking Tour and Scotch Whisky Experience are both within easy walking distance of Old Town accommodation. Book The Witchery and Ondine well in advance as they are highly sought-after. September in Edinburgh can be crisp and occasionally rainy — pack a quality waterproof layer.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle Tour: Begin the day with a private guided tour of Edinburgh Castle, the iconic fortress perched dramatically on volcanic rock overlooking the city. Explore the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, the Great Hall, and the Royal Palace at your own premium pace with an expert historian guide, avoiding the general crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underground Vaults & Ghost Tour (afternoon private session): Descend into the eerie 18th-century South Bridge Vaults hidden beneath the city streets. A private afternoon session allows for a more intimate and detailed exploration of these historically rich chambers, with your guide recounting tales of crime, poverty, and the supernatural that once filled these hidden spaces.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Tasting at The Whiski Rooms: Conclude the day with a curated guided tasting session at The Whiski Rooms on North Bank Street, one of Edinburgh's finest whisky bars. Sample five premium expressions — from peaty Islay malts to elegant Speyside drams — guided by a knowledgeable whisky specialist who can tailor the selection to your palate.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your luxury Old Town property — opt for the full Scottish breakfast featuring smoked salmon, Stornoway black pudding, and freshly baked pastries.
meals.lunch: Cannonball Restaurant & Bar — situated in a historic 16th-century building at the top of the Royal Mile, offering refined Scottish comfort food including haggis bon bons and slow-cooked venison, with stunning castle views.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Martin Wishart (Edinburgh outpost or The Honours) — a Michelin-starred dining experience showcasing the finest Scottish produce with French-influenced technique. An exceptional pairing with the whisky-focused evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Edinburgh Castle private tour early in the morning to enjoy it before peak visitor hours. The Underground Vaults private afternoon session should be pre-booked directly. The Whiski Rooms tasting can be arranged as a private session for a more personalised experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the castle grounds involve cobblestones and inclines.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to the Scottish Highlands and a distillery visit: Depart early by private chauffeur for a scenic drive to The Glenkinchie Distillery (Lowland) or, for a longer premium experience, head north to Perthhouse-area distilleries such as Glenturret — Scotland's oldest working distillery. Enjoy an exclusive behind-the-scenes distillery tour, including warehousing, the still room, and a private cask tasting with the master distiller.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the distillery experience with a private cask selection session and a gourmet distillery lunch before returning to Edinburgh by mid-afternoon. En route back, stop at a scenic Highland viewpoint for photography and to absorb the dramatic September landscape of heather-covered moorland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Edinburgh Old Town. Enjoy a relaxed evening stroll through Grassmarket and the Cowgate, soaking in the atmospheric Old Town ambience as the gas-lit closes and medieval architecture glow in the early autumn dusk.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast at the hotel before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Private gourmet lunch at the distillery — many premium Scottish distilleries offer exclusive dining experiences paired with their whiskies. Alternatively, The Glenturret Lalique Restaurant holds Michelin-star status and offers an extraordinary whisky-and-food pairing menu.
meals.dinner: The Kitchin, Tom Kitchin's flagship Michelin-starred restaurant in Leith (a short private transfer from Old Town) — celebrating 'From Nature to Plate' philosophy with outstanding Scottish seasonal ingredients and an exceptional wine and whisky list.

day_by_day.notes: This day requires a private chauffeur for the full day — arrange in advance. Glenturret's Lalique Restaurant requires reservations months ahead. If Glenturret is fully booked, Glenkinchie is a shorter drive (30 minutes from Edinburgh) and offers premium tour options. September heather bloom makes the Highland scenery particularly spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Palace of Holyroodhouse & Arthur's Seat: Visit the Palace of Holyroodhouse, the official Scottish residence of the monarch, at the foot of the Royal Mile. Arrange a private guided tour exploring the State Apartments, the historic chambers of Mary Queen of Scots, and the ruins of Holyrood Abbey. Afterwards, take a private guided walk up Arthur's Seat — the ancient volcanic peak within Holyrood Park — for panoramic views over Edinburgh and the Firth of Forth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dean Village & Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art: Transfer by private car to the picturesque Dean Village, a hidden gem along the Water of Leith. Stroll the tranquil riverside walkway before visiting the Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art, which houses an exceptional collection of 20th-century Scottish and international art in a grand neoclassical building.
day_by_day.evening: Private whisky blending masterclass: Return to the Old Town for an exclusive private whisky blending experience hosted by a master blender — available through specialist operators in Edinburgh. Create your own bespoke blended Scotch whisky to take home as a personalised souvenir of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Scottish breakfast at the hotel — smoked haddock kedgeree, Loch Fyne kippers, or a traditional cooked spread.
meals.lunch: Cafe St Honoré — a charming French-Scottish bistro in the New Town, celebrated for its market-driven menu, outstanding cheese board, and thoughtful wine list. A refined and intimate lunch setting.
meals.dinner: Number One at The Balmoral Hotel — Edinburgh's most celebrated fine dining restaurant, holding a Michelin star and offering an exquisite tasting menu of Scottish produce. The sommelier's whisky pairing option is a highlight not to be missed.

day_by_day.notes: The Palace of Holyroodhouse is occasionally closed for Royal engagements — confirm availability before the trip. The climb to Arthur's Seat takes approximately 45 minutes and is moderate in difficulty; wear appropriate footwear. The private whisky blending masterclass should be pre-booked through operators such as 'The Wee Distillery' or specialist concierge services. Number One at The Balmoral requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the New Town & Georgian Heritage: Begin with a leisurely morning exploring Edinburgh's Georgian New Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit Charlotte Square and Georgian House (a beautifully restored 18th-century townhouse) for insight into Edinburgh's elegant past. Browse the upscale boutiques and independent shops along Thistle Street and Stockbridge for premium Scottish gifts — cashmere, Harris Tweed, and artisan whisky accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scottish National Museum: Spend the early afternoon at the National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — a world-class museum covering Scottish history, culture, science, and the natural world. The Whisky Gallery and the medieval Scottish artefacts are particularly aligned with the trip's themes. Afterwards, enjoy a final leisurely walk through Greyfriars Kirkyard, one of Edinburgh's most atmospheric historic graveyards.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final dram: Conclude the premium Edinburgh experience with a celebratory farewell dinner followed by a nightcap at a legendary Edinburgh whisky bar.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in your hotel suite or at the hotel's fine dining restaurant — a fitting send-off for the final morning.
meals.lunch: The Pompadour by Galvin at the Waldorf Astoria Edinburgh (The Caledonian) — a stunning Edwardian dining room serving classic French-Scottish cuisine with impeccable service and an extensive wine cellar.
meals.dinner: Timberyard — a pioneering farm-to-table restaurant in a converted Victorian warehouse in the Grassmarket area, offering a seasonal tasting menu with outstanding Scottish produce, foraged ingredients, and a remarkable natural wine and whisky selection. After dinner, enjoy a final nightcap at The Scotch Whisky Experience members' bar or the atmospheric Bow Bar on Victoria Street, renowned for its exceptional range of rare single malts.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your personally blended whisky from Day 4 securely for travel. The Georgian House on Charlotte Square is managed by the National Trust for Scotland — check seasonal opening hours. Timberyard is very popular and should be reserved well in advance. If departing the following morning, arrange a chauffeur transfer to Edinburgh Airport in advance. Consider purchasing a bottle of rare Scotch from Royal Mile Whiskies or Cadenhead's on the Royal Mile as a premium memento of the trip.

query: Edinburgh history and whisky, $2000 solo, 5 days, September 2027, from London
